h1:
Where to Stay in Pai?
12 Hotels We've Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites
heroSub: Twelve Pai hotels across every budget — 5-star riverside resorts and rice-field villas with mountain views, down to value bungalows and a hostel. Covering the three main areas: in-town near the Walking Street, by the Pai River, and the rice fields with mountain views. Starting from around ฿350–7,500/night.
introH2: 🏞️ Why does choosing the right area in Pai matter?
introHtml: Pai is a small town in a valley, but the areas you can stay in feel distinctly different — in-town Pai is walking distance to the Walking Street with its evening food and stalls, the most convenient base if you don't have a vehicle · by the Pai River is quieter, you wake up to water views, and some spots let you cross a bridge into town · while the rice fields with mountain views (Mae Hi / Mae Na Thoeng) are open, peaceful stays best for those with a vehicle who want a proper retreat, but you'll need to drive into town. Many travellers book without checking where they are, then spend the whole trip driving or taking motorbike taxis back and forth. This guide brings together 12 Pai hotels we've reviewed across every tier — from luxury riverside resorts down to value bungalows and a hostel. Every pick comes from reading real guest reviews, with prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links throughout.
mrtHtml: Pai has no city-style public transport — the main ways to get around are renting a scooter, walking, or taking a songthaew/motorbike taxi within town. Most travellers reach Pai by minivan from Chiang Mai (about 3 hours over the famous 762 curves) and then get around on foot or by rented scooter. The areas in this guide: in-town Pai — walk to the Walking Street, restaurants, cafes (The Quarter, Yoma, Pai Village, B2 Pai, Common Grounds) · by the Pai River — quiet, water views, some within a bridge of town (Reverie Siam, Baan Krating, Baan Pai Riverside) · rice fields with mountain views (Mae Hi / Mae Na Thoeng) — open views, peaceful, best with a vehicle (Puri Pai, Phu Pai, Pai My Guest, Pairadise).

entries.name: Reverie Siam Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 By the Pai River · walk to the Walking Street
entries.addr: 476 Moo 8, Wiang Tai, Pai, Mae Hong Son 58130
entries.storyHtml: The highest score in this guide at 9.5 — Reverie Siam is Pai's top-tier luxury resort, built around a 1920s colonial design on the banks of the Pai River. Reviews most often mention the saltwater pool, the riverside garden setting, and the attentive service. The sweet spot is staying riverside and quiet yet still able to walk to the Walking Street — ideal for a special-occasion trip or honeymoon.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If the budget allows, choose a Deluxe Pool View or a Villa — reviews keep mentioning the riverside atmosphere at dusk — and rooms fill fast in the cool high season, so book ahead.
pros: Highest score in the guide, 9.5 · distinctive colonial design
Riverside Pai River location, quiet yet walkable to the Walking Street
Saltwater pool and riverside garden that reviews love
Luxury-level, attentive service — great for couples
cons: Highest price in this guide — best for a special trip
Cool high season pushes prices up and rooms sell out fast

entries.name: The Quarter Pai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Central Pai · walk to the Walking Street
entries.addr: 245 Moo 1 Chaisongkram Road, Wiang Tai, Pai, Mae Hong Son 58130
entries.storyHtml: The Quarter is a boutique resort in central Pai scoring a high 9.2. Reviews most often praise the location — a few minutes' walk to the Walking Street — the clean, spacious rooms, and the swimming pool. Rooms start at ฿1,400 and range from Superior to a Family Room, so it suits families too. A great fit if you want to be in the heart of town without needing a vehicle.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room on the pool side, which is quieter than the Chaisongkram Road side, and groups should pick the Family Room — better value than booking two rooms.
pros: Central Pai location, the easiest walk to the Walking Street in this guide
High 9.2 score · clean, spacious rooms that reviews like
Has a swimming pool — good for relaxing in town
Family Rooms available for families
cons: The Superior is a No View room — pick Deluxe for a garden view
In the centre of town, the Walking Street can be lively on weekend nights

entries.name: Yoma Hotel Pai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Near the Walking Street · free shuttle
entries.addr: 59 Moo 1, Wiang Tai, Pai, Mae Hong Son 58130
entries.storyHtml: Yoma is the best-value in-town hotel in this price band — from just ฿900 yet scoring 9.1. Reviews most often mention the free shuttle (very handy if you arrive by minivan with no scooter), the location near the Walking Street, and the clean rooms. Higher floors get rice-field and mountain views. A good fit for budget travellers who still want to be near town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Book a Deluxe or above for a rice-field view, and ask about the free shuttle times when you book — it saves on motorbike-taxi fares around town.
pros: Excellent starting price ฿900 · high 9.1 score
Free shuttle service — handy without your own vehicle
Near the Walking Street, walkable for sightseeing
Higher floors have rice-field and mountain views
cons: The entry Superior has no view — pick Deluxe for one
A small hotel — fewer facilities than a big resort

entries.name: Pairadise
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Baan Mae Yen · bamboo bridge into town
entries.addr: 98 Moo 1, Baan Mae Yen, Mae Hi, Pai 58130
entries.storyHtml: Pairadise is a great-value rice-field bungalow stay scoring a high 9.1 from 238 reviews. Reviews most often mention the natural spring pool, the fish pond, the shady garden and the peaceful atmosphere. A favourite detail is being able to walk across a bamboo bridge and rice fields into town. Rooms start at just ฿850 yet you get full nature surroundings — ideal for laid-back travellers and couples.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Swim in the natural pool mid-morning when the sun's out and the water is clearest, and cross the bamboo bridge at dusk for the rice-field views into town.
pros: High 9.1 score · excellent starting price ฿850
Natural spring pool, fish pond and shady garden that reviews love
Walk across the bamboo bridge and rice fields into town
Peaceful atmosphere, balcony hammocks — great for chilling
cons: A 2-star bungalow stay focused on atmosphere — no big-resort facilities
On the rice-field side — walkable to town but further than in-town stays

entries.name: Pai Village Boutique Resort & Farm
entries.mrtTag: 📍 In-town Pai · walk to the Walking Street
entries.addr: 88 Moo 3, Vieng Tai, Pai, Mae Hong Son 58130
entries.storyHtml: Pai Village is the most-reviewed boutique in this guide — nearly 2,000 reviews — scoring 9.0. Reviews most often praise the Lanna-style wooden rooms set in a green garden right in town, the shady, leafy atmosphere, and the easy walk to the Walking Street. It ranges from garden rooms to cottages by the Pai River. A good fit if you want a Lanna feel while still being able to walk into town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a water view choose the Riverfront Cottage, and the garden rooms are lovely for a cool-morning coffee on the porch.
pros: Most reviewed in the guide, nearly 2,000 reviews · 9.0 score
Lanna-style wooden rooms in a green garden that reviews love
In-town location, walk to the Walking Street
Riverside cottages by the Pai River available
cons: Riverside rooms cost more and sell out fast — book ahead
A larger resort — busier than the small boutiques

entries.name: Common Grounds Pai
entries.mrtTag: 📍 In-town Pai · near the Walking Street
entries.storyHtml: Common Grounds is the cheapest stay in this guide from just ฿350, yet scoring 8.8 — very high for a hostel. Reviews most often mention the social atmosphere that makes it easy to meet people, the air-conditioned dorms with lockers, and the location just ~50m from the Walking Street. There are private bungalows for those who want more privacy. Ideal for solo travellers and backpackers on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want privacy but still in town, the private bungalow is still better value than many hotels, and dorm rates rise in the cool late-year season, so book ahead.
pros: Cheapest in the guide ฿350 · high 8.8 score for a hostel
Social atmosphere, easy to meet people — great solo
Air-con dorms with lockers · ~50m from the Walking Street
Private bungalows available if you want more privacy
cons: A social hostel — some bar/social noise, not for those wanting quiet
Dorms use shared bathrooms, not suited to families with young kids

entries.name: Pai My Guest Resort
entries.addr: 100 Moo 1, Baan Mae Yen, Mae Hi, Pai 58130
entries.storyHtml: Pai My Guest is a good-value rice-field bungalow resort scoring 8.7 from 209 reviews. Reviews most often mention the swimming pool, the rice-field and mountain views, and the peaceful feel close to town. It ranges from garden bungalows to a family villa. A good fit if you want the rice-field atmosphere without being too far from town, from just ฿900.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The Field/Mountain View bungalow is only a little more than the Garden View but opens up the view, and a vehicle helps — in town, a motorbike taxi or scooter is easier.
pros: Good starting price ฿900 · 8.7 score
Has a swimming pool — rare for a rice-field stay at this price
Open rice-field and mountain views that reviews love
Family villa available for groups
cons: On the rice-field side — near town but easier with a vehicle
The entry Garden View bungalow has less of an open view than the field-view rooms

entries.name: Puri Pai Villa Wellness & Retreat
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mae Hi rice fields · mountain views
entries.addr: 130 Moo 5, Mae Na Thoeng, Pai, Mae Hong Son 58130
entries.storyHtml: Puri Pai is a luxury wellness-retreat villa on the rice fields with mountain views, scoring 8.7. Reviews most often mention the private pool villas, the onsen, and the open mountain views. It ranges from Deluxe mountain-view rooms up to private pool villas for groups. The sweet spot is the peaceful, private feel on a hillside above the fields — best for a proper retreat and for those with a vehicle.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Groups or anyone wanting a private pool should pick the 1-Bedroom Pool Villa, and as it sits on a rice-field hillside, a private vehicle helps for getting in and out of town.
pros: Private pool villas and an onsen that reviews love
Open mountain views on the rice fields, quiet and private
Several room tiers, from Deluxe up to group pool villas
Wellness atmosphere — great for a proper retreat
cons: On a Mae Na Thoeng rice-field hillside, far from town — best with a vehicle
The entry Deluxe has no private pool — you'd step up to a pool villa

entries.name: Phu Pai Art Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Rice fields with mountain views · Mae Na Thoeng
entries.addr: 92 Moo 1, Mae Na Thoeng, Pai, Mae Hong Son 58130
entries.storyHtml: Phu Pai is a boutique resort of adobe-earth villas set among the rice fields with mountain views, scoring 8.4. Reviews most often mention the distinctive earthen-villa design, the open rice-field and mountain views, and the sense of privacy. It ranges from Superior Villa up to a Honeymoon Suite for couples. A good fit if you love a quiet rice-field setting and design — best with a vehicle for getting into town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Couples should pick the Honeymoon Suite or Phupai Suite for the more open view, and an early-morning mist over the rice fields in the cool season is a highlight reviews mention.
pros: Distinctive adobe-earth villa design that reviews love
Open rice-field and mountain views, quiet and private
Honeymoon Suite available for couples
Every room is a villa with a private balcony
cons: On the Mae Na Thoeng rice fields, far from town — best with a vehicle
Focused on atmosphere and design — fewer facilities than a big resort

entries.name: Baan Pai Riverside
entries.mrtTag: 📍 By the Pai River · in town
entries.storyHtml: Baan Pai Riverside is an accessible wooden riverside bungalow stay with a large 416 reviews, scoring 8.4. Reviews most often mention the riverside location in town, the wooden bungalows with water-view balconies, and the prices starting from just ฿500. There are both fan and air-con rooms. A favourite detail is crossing the bridge into the Pai Walking Street — a good fit for budget travellers who want a riverside feel in town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For a water view pick a River View bungalow, and nights get cold in the cool season — a fan room is fine, but choose an air-con bungalow if you prefer A/C.
pros: Large review count, 416 · very low starting price ฿500
Riverside Pai River location in town, water-view atmosphere
Cross the bridge into the Pai Walking Street
Both fan and air-con rooms to suit the budget
cons: Simple wooden bungalows — no resort-style facilities
The entry fan bungalow has no A/C — pick Deluxe for air-con

entries.name: B2 Pai Premier Resort
entries.badge: 🏊 Pool · walk to the Walking Street
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Walk to the Walking Street · has a pool
entries.addr: 76 Moo 2, Wiang Tai, Pai, Mae Hong Son 58130
entries.storyHtml: B2 Pai is a 3-star resort from the B2 group with a large 897 reviews, scoring 8.0. Reviews most often mention the low starting price, the swimming pool, and the location within walking distance of the Walking Street. As a chain, the room standard is fairly consistent. A good fit for budget travellers who want a pool and a hotel feel over a bungalow, though the score is middling — pick a renovated room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose the Deluxe Pool View for the pool view and a room in better condition than the entry rooms, and it's only a few minutes' walk to the Walking Street.
pros: Large review count 897 · low starting price ฿750
Has a swimming pool — rare at this price
B2 group, a fairly consistent room standard
Walkable to the Walking Street
cons: Middling 8.0 score · some rooms show their age — pick a renovated one
A chain hotel — less character than the Pai boutiques

entries.name: Baan Krating Pai Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 By the Pai River · in the foothills
entries.addr: 358 Moo 8, Wiang Tai, Pai, Mae Hong Son 58130
entries.storyHtml: Baan Krating is a boutique resort of riverside bungalows in the Pai foothills, scoring 8.0. Reviews most often mention the quiet riverside-and-foothills location, the bungalows with garden and mountain-view balconies, and the natural atmosphere. It ranges from Deluxe to Family rooms. A good fit for those who want a quiet riverside stay away from the bustle in town — review count is still modest but the natural setting stands out, and a vehicle helps.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick the Deluxe Pavilion, a bungalow with a private balcony and a more open view, and as it leans into foothill quiet, a vehicle helps for reaching the Walking Street.
pros: Quiet riverside-and-foothills location, a natural setting
Bungalows with garden and mountain-view balconies that reviews like
Family rooms available for groups
Good for those escaping the bustle in town
cons: Still few reviews (110) versus others on the list
Leans into foothill quiet, away from the Walking Street — best with a vehicle

adviceTitle: How to pick the right Pai hotel for you

advice.head: Tight budget, best value
advice.bodyHtml: → Common Grounds Pai ฿350, an in-town hostel · or Baan Pai Riverside ฿500, riverside bungalows · or Yoma Hotel Pai ฿900, near the Walking Street with a free shuttle

advice.head: Special trip, a luxury resort
advice.bodyHtml: → Reverie Siam Resort ฿4,800, riverside luxury scoring 9.5 · or Puri Pai Villa ฿2,800, wellness pool villas with mountain views

advice.head: No vehicle, want to be in town
advice.bodyHtml: → The Quarter Pai ฿1,400, central, walk to the Walking Street · or Pai Village ฿1,800, an in-town boutique in a green garden

advice.head: Travelling as a family with kids
advice.bodyHtml: → The Quarter Pai ฿1,400, Family Rooms in town · or Pai My Guest Resort ฿900, a family villa and a pool

advice.head: Romantic trip, couples
advice.bodyHtml: → Reverie Siam Resort ฿4,800, riverside colonial style · or Phu Pai Art Resort ฿2,200, adobe villas with a Honeymoon Suite

advice.head: Want rice fields and mountain views
advice.bodyHtml: → Puri Pai Villa ฿2,800, pool villas with mountain views · or Phu Pai Art Resort ฿2,200, adobe villas in the rice fields · or Pai My Guest ฿900, rice-field bungalows with a pool

advice.head: Want to stay by the Pai River
advice.bodyHtml: → Reverie Siam Resort ฿4,800, riverside luxury near the Walking Street · or Baan Pai Riverside ฿500, budget riverside bungalows · or Baan Krating Pai ฿1,800, quiet riverside-foothill bungalows

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Pai hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in in Pai?
faq.a: It depends on whether you have a vehicle · In-town Pai suits those without a vehicle who want to walk to the Walking Street, restaurants and cafes (The Quarter, Yoma, Pai Village, B2 Pai, Common Grounds) · by the Pai River suits those who want a quieter, water-view atmosphere (Reverie Siam, Baan Krating, Baan Pai Riverside) · the rice fields with mountain views at Mae Hi / Mae Na Thoeng suit those with a vehicle who want a peaceful, open-view retreat (Puri Pai, Phu Pai, Pai My Guest, Pairadise).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Pai hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: hostels and bungalows start around ฿350–900/night · in-town hotels and 3–4-star boutiques run about ฿900–2,800 · luxury resorts and pool villas start ฿2,800–7,500 · Pai rates swing clearly with the season, and in the cool late-year months and on long weekends prices can be much higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Pai hotel?
faq.a: For normal periods, booking 2–4 weeks ahead is enough · but in the cool late-year season (Nov–Jan), on long weekends and over New Year, the good rooms sell out fast — Pai is a small town with limited rooms — so book 1–2 months ahead or more, especially for riverside stays and luxury resorts.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest to book a Pai hotel?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary by promotion at different times — we recommend comparing all 3 before every booking. Each review page in this guide has price-comparison links, which can save you hundreds of baht per night.

faq.q: ❓ Do I need a motorbike in Pai?
faq.a: It depends on where you stay · if you stay in-town Pai you can easily walk to the Walking Street and in-town spots, so a vehicle isn't essential · but if you stay on the rice fields, mountain side or in the foothills (Puri Pai, Phu Pai, Baan Krating), or want to visit spots around town like Pai Canyon, waterfalls and the Memorial Bridge, renting a scooter or having a vehicle is far more convenient · some hotels offer a shuttle or scooter rental — ask when you book.

faq.q: ❓ How do I get from Chiang Mai to Pai?
faq.a: The most popular way is the minivan from Chiang Mai to Pai, taking about 3 hours over the famous 762 curves (bring motion-sickness tablets if you're prone to it) · vans run several times a day from Chiang Mai's Arcade bus station · or drive/ride yourself along Highway 1095 · some people fly from Chiang Mai to Pai's airport, but flights are few and unreliable, so the minivan is more convenient and better value.
